public_rationale: On October 13, 2026, the IMF described financial markets as resilient and an AI-related correction as a possible source of future stress. [e1] That assessment does not establish the broad AI investment collapse required to test this forecast. [e1] It also provides no evidence of the subsequent survival or disappearance of the relevant compute customers. [e1]
limitations: The forecast gives no deadline, objective collapse threshold or post-collapse observation period.
The evidence does not define the baseline customer population or verify that it is predominantly unprofitable and venture-backed.
The IMF assessment does not establish whether a qualifying collapse occurred by October 28, 2026.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Once the AI bubble bursts, the mostly unprofitable venture-backed customers of AI compute will no longer exist.

statement.excerpt: The difference will be that once the AI bubble bursts, the customers of AI compute — predominantly unprofitable, venture-backed startups — won’t exist.

our_interpretation: This is a conditional forecast with no stated deadline. The nearby 2030 cost comparison does not supply a deadline for this sentence.
The plain reading is a broad disappearance of the current venture-backed compute-customer population after an AI investment collapse, not the failure of one startup.
A bubble burst requires evidence of a broad collapse in AI investment and valuations. A temporary price decline or an individual financing problem is insufficient.
Won't exist means ceasing business operations. Acquisition, restructuring or a name change alone does not establish disappearance of compute demand.
Predominantly unprofitable and venture-backed describes the baseline customer population and needs independent verification.
criteria.support_condition: After the triggering collapse is established, business-survival records show that the described customer population has broadly ceased operating.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the triggering collapse and its aftermath are established, a substantial continuing population of the same customers remains operational and continues purchasing compute.

evidence.locator: Opening report summary, before Athanasios Vamvakidis's remarks
evidence.explanation: The accompanying remarks describe an AI-related correction as a possible future shock. This does not establish that the trigger happened, nor rule out every possible interpretation of a bubble burst through October 28.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Evidence dating a broad collapse in AI investment and valuations, followed by operating and compute-purchasing records for a defined pre-collapse customer population. Those records must show broad disappearance or substantial continued operation.
